title: Invoice Capacity and Add-On Settings of Each Patient Payment Plans Term
content:
Each term of **Patient Payment Plans** carries a fixed invoice capacity and a set of settings for invoices joining a plan after it has been accepted. The schedule lists them for all six terms.

| Term | Most invoices one plan may carry over its life | New eligible invoice may be added after acceptance | Re-amortize on add (term setting) | Add-on extension months |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Payment Plan | 3 | No | No | 0 |
| 6-Month Payment Plan | 5 | Yes | Yes | 0 |
| 9-Month Payment Plan | 6 | Yes | Yes | 3 |
| 12-Month Payment Plan | 8 | Yes | Yes | 3 |
| 18-Month Payment Plan | 10 | Yes | Yes | 6 |
| 24-Month Extended Payment Plan | 12 | Yes | Yes | 0 |

## Definitions

- **Most invoices over its life** counts every invoice the plan has ever carried, not only those still on it.
- **May be added after acceptance** states whether a new eligible invoice may be put on a plan that the patient has already accepted. On the 3-Month Payment Plan it may not; the invoices of a 3-Month plan are those enrolled before acceptance.
- **Re-amortize on add** is the term's recorded setting on whether adding an invoice recomputes the installment over the remaining installments.
- **Add-on extension months** is the number of months by which adding invoices may extend the original term; 0 means none. The 9-Month and 12-Month terms carry 3, the 18-Month term carries 6, and the 3-Month, 6-Month and 24-Month Extended terms carry none.

## Examples (hypothetical plans)

- A 6-Month Payment Plan that has already carried 5 invoices has reached its capacity; a sixth invoice cannot join it, even if one of the five has since been paid off.
- A 12-Month Payment Plan carrying 3 invoices may take on a fourth, subject to the plan's other enrollment conditions.
